section_summary: This section documents U.S. State Department economic, educational, and administrative planning for occupied Japan and Korea between September 1945 and August 1946. Key subjects include Japanese anti-inflationary currency and financial controls, zaibatsu dissolution, educational reorientation, and economic assessments of the loss of overseas territories including Manchuria, Formosa, and Korea. The papers also cover Allied collation of enemy assets, private trade inquiries, and the recruitment, logistics, and financing for Arthur C. Bunce's Economic Advisory Mission to Korea.

subfiles.about: Discusses Commerce Department economic intelligence interests and personnel assignments in occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: Moser and Willoughby discuss Commerce Department economic intelligence needs, commodity requirements, and potential officer assignments in Japan.
subfiles.title: Interests of the Department of Commerce in Economic Work by the Office of the Political Adviser to SCAP

subfiles.about: Reviews the development of policies and interdepartmental committees regarding Japanese educational reform.
subfiles.summary: Traces State Department policy formulation on Japanese educational reform since early 1944. It describes interdepartmental cooperation with the Army, SWNCC directives, textbook procurement for GHQ Tokyo, and a September 1945 consultation with outside specialists. It recommends establishing permanent staffing and cultural cooperation programs.
subfiles.title: Status of Policies Relating to Education and Reeducation in Japan

subfiles.about: Endorses recruiting qualified economic specialists for Japan and recounts wartime experiences.
subfiles.summary: Géauque praises Vincent's broadcast on recruiting economic specialists for Japan and recounts his wartime work in the Board of Economic Warfare.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin P. Géauque to John Carter Vincent Regarding Economic Experts for Japan

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Géauque's letter regarding Vincent's radio broadcast on Japanese economic experts.
subfiles.summary: Penfield conveys appreciation for Géauque's comments, noting Vincent could not reply personally due to departure for the Moscow Conference.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. K. Penfield to Edwin P. Géauque Acknowledging Broadcast Comments

subfiles.about: Describes the role and procedure of the informal Committee on Economic Policy toward Japan.
subfiles.summary: Outlines the informal committee assisting Edwin M. Martin in drafting SWNCC economic policies and evaluating occupation issues.
subfiles.title: Committee on Economic Policy toward Japan

subfiles.about: Reports the arrival of W. Willoughby in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson reports Willoughby's arrival in Tokyo on October 20 and requests notification of his family.
subfiles.title: Telegram Announcing Arrival of Willoughby in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Confirms the selection of James M. Henderson for an economic mission to dissolve Japanese combines.
subfiles.summary: Secretary Byrnes informs Senator Connally that Henderson was selected for the mission recommending policies to dissolve Japanese business combines.
subfiles.title: Letter from James F. Byrnes to Senator Tom Connally Regarding James M. Henderson

subfiles.about: Transmits labor correspondence from Assistant Secretary Clayton to Edwin M. Martin.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Michael Ross's correspondence on labor policy to Martin for appropriate action.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip from Will Clayton to Edwin M. Martin

subfiles.about: Expresses CIO interest in occupation labor policy and transmits a copy of a letter to General Hilldring.
subfiles.summary: Ross transmits his letter to General Hilldring urging consultation with American labor organizations regarding occupation labor policies.
subfiles.title: Letter from Michael Ross to Will Clayton Concerning Occupation Labor Policy

subfiles.about: Urges Army consultation with labor organizations regarding survey missions and labor policies in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Ross advocates consultation with organized labor concerning personnel and policies for upcoming Army labor missions to Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Michael Ross to Major General John Hilldring on Japanese Labor Policy

subfiles.about: Transmits Senator Connally's referral concerning James M. Henderson to Edwin M. Martin.
subfiles.summary: Routes Senator Connally's referral and attached Henderson telegram to Martin for appropriate action.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip from Will Clayton to Edwin M. Martin on Connally Referral

subfiles.about: Transmits a telegram from James M. Henderson endorsing his appointment to an economic survey mission.
subfiles.summary: Refers James M. Henderson's telegram requesting appointment to the economic policy mission to Will Clayton.
subfiles.title: Referral Slip from Senator Tom Connally to Will Clayton

subfiles.about: Solicits Senator Connally's support for appointment to the State Department economic policy mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Henderson requests Connally's backing for a top position on the economic survey mission leaving for Japan.
subfiles.title: Telegram from James McInnes Henderson to Senator Tom Connally

subfiles.about: Welcomes CIO consultation and discussions on U.S. labor policies in Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: Martin acknowledges Ross's letter, commends recent discussions, and invites ongoing suggestions regarding labor policy in Japan and Korea.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to Michael Ross Regarding Labor Policy

subfiles.about: Requests expanded economic coverage, specifically regarding cooperatives and waterpower, in weekly summaries from Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Martin asks Atcheson to provide more economic information in weekly summaries, particularly regarding cooperative unions and waterpower development.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to George A. Atcheson, Jr. on Economic Reporting

subfiles.about: Transmits documents proposing Allied collation of data on Japanese economic penetration and assets.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a British aide-mémoire regarding Allied cooperation in investigating and collating data on Japanese economic penetration and assets.
subfiles.title: Diplomatic Note to the Chinese Ambassador on Japanese Economic Penetration

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of U.S. note regarding Allied collation of Japanese economic penetration data.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt of the U.S. communication enclosing British documents concerning Japanese economic penetration.
subfiles.title: Diplomatic Note from Chinese Embassy Acknowledging Communication on Economic Penetration

subfiles.about: Inquires about obtaining an official permit to participate in post-war building reconstruction in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Day requests instructions and permit applications to trade with the enemy for rebuilding homes and structures in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Margaret C. Day Requesting Permit to Trade with Japan

subfiles.about: Informs Day that her inquiry regarding trading with Japan was forwarded to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.summary: Hibbard informs Day that her permit application was referred to Treasury Foreign Funds Control.
subfiles.title: Speedletter from Richard E. Hibbard to Margaret C. Day

subfiles.about: Discusses distribution of economic intelligence and commends Federal Reserve research on Japanese foreign trade.
subfiles.summary: Martin explains document shortages, suggests contacting Colonel Proudfoot, and praises Arthur Hersey's study on future Japanese trade.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to Wendell E. Thorne on Economic Materials

subfiles.about: Requests State Department reports on Japanese and Korean financial and economic developments.
subfiles.summary: Thorne expresses thanks for trade statistics and requests copies of reports on Japanese and Korean economic and financial trends.
subfiles.title: Letter from Wendell E. Thorne to Edwin M. Martin Requesting Economic Reports

subfiles.about: Concurs in principle with British proposal to establish an agency in Tokyo to collate enemy and looted assets.
subfiles.summary: The Chinese Ambassador agrees to the proposal to create an organization in Tokyo collating data on United Nations and enemy assets.
subfiles.title: Diplomatic Note from Chinese Ambassador Regarding Allied Collation of Enemy Assets

subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum evaluating emergency anti-inflationary economic controls enacted in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Bishop reports on six emergency Imperial Ordinances freezing bank deposits and converting currency, assessing political reactions and enforcement prospects.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 277 Transmitting Memorandum on Emergency Economic Controls

subfiles.about: Analyzes Imperial Ordinances Nos. 83-88 designed to curb inflation, collect food, and survey hidden property.
subfiles.summary: Blakemore details six emergency ordinances enacted February 17, 1946, freezing bank accounts, recalling currency, requisitioning grains, and surveying property. He evaluates reactions across Japanese political parties, press commentary, and initial business and market consequences.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Emergency Economic Controls of February 17, 1946
subfiles.to: Office of the United States Political Adviser

subfiles.about: Requests an export allotment of Japanese textiles and blankets for a firm in Nova Goa.
subfiles.summary: Casa Utamchand applies for an export quota of Japanese yard goods and plush blankets based on prewar business.
subfiles.title: Letter from Casa Utamchand Requesting Import Allotments from Japan

subfiles.about: Instructs the Consul General on official channels and restrictions governing Japanese export trade.
subfiles.summary: Explains that private commercial trade with Japan is prohibited, exports are handled by official agencies, and textile supplies remain very tight.
subfiles.title: Instruction to American Consul General at Bombay Regarding Trade with Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits translation of a Japanese periodical article on the economic impact of losing overseas territories.
subfiles.summary: Service transmits an ATIS translation of an article from Economist analyzing the consequences of Japan's loss of empire.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 294 Transmitting Translation of Magazine Article on Loss of Overseas Territory

subfiles.about: Translates a Japanese economic analysis assessing the catastrophic impact of losing colonial resources and territories.
subfiles.from: Allied Translator and Interpreter Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: This translation of an article from Economist analyzes the loss of Manchuria, Formosa, Korea, Karafuto, and South Pacific islands. It details how Japanese industrial growth relied on colonial agricultural exports, mining wealth, and zaibatsu investments. The study concludes that Japanese economic revival requires complete reconstruction on new foundations.
subfiles.title: ATIS Press Translation No. 1624: Loss of Overseas Territories and Effect upon Japan's Economy

subfiles.about: Designates a permanent record replacement copy of telegram C-60050 for central files.
subfiles.summary: Document replacement sheet substituting white copy for unreturned yellow copy of telegram C-60050.
subfiles.title: Document Record Replacement Sheet for Telegram C-60050

subfiles.about: Recommends extending Dr. Gordon Strong's assignment to the Bunce Economic Mission in Korea.
subfiles.summary: CINCAFPAC relays USAMGIK request to extend Dr. Strong's assignment in Korea to support the Joint Commission and import programs.
subfiles.title: Telegram C-60050 on Extension of Assignment for Dr. Gordon Strong

subfiles.about: Records verification of a shipment of supplies destined for the Political Adviser in Seoul, Korea.
subfiles.summary: Standard form recording ten boxes of supplies shipped via San Francisco to Seoul.
subfiles.title: Standard Form Shipping Note on Bunce Mission Supplies

subfiles.about: Reports that supplies for the Bunce Mission were missing upon vessel discharge in Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson reports that supplies intended for the Bunce Mission were not found aboard ship upon unloading in Yokohama.
subfiles.title: Telegram C-60028 Regarding Missing Bunce Mission Supplies

subfiles.about: Reports that search of the vessel located three boxes of supplies for the Bunce Mission.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson reports finding several boxes containing typewriters and supplies, which are being forwarded to Seoul by freight.
subfiles.title: Telegram 184 on Partial Recovery of Bunce Mission Supplies

subfiles.about: Directs Despatch Agent Horan to investigate missing shipment of Bunce Mission supplies.
subfiles.summary: Havens instructs Horan to investigate the disappearance of ten supply boxes billed for the Bunce Mission.
subfiles.title: Telegram Sent to U.S. Despatch Agent Investigating Bunce Mission Supplies

subfiles.about: Urges General Hilldring to request Federal Reserve Board approval extending Arthur C. Bunce's leave.
subfiles.summary: Galbraith notes Bunce's vital role with General Hodge and urges Hilldring to ask Marriner Eccles to extend Bunce's leave.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Extension of Arthur C. Bunce's Assignment in Korea

subfiles.about: Relays General Hodge's urgent request to retain Arthur C. Bunce as economic advisor in Korea.
subfiles.summary: General Hodge requests Bunce and his staff be retained indefinitely to support the Joint Commission and Military Government in Korea.
subfiles.title: War Department Telegram C-60474 Relaying General Hodge's Request to Retain Bunce

subfiles.about: Requests a meeting with Governor Szymczak and Chairman Eccles regarding Bunce's leave of absence.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring asks Szymczak and Eccles to extend Bunce's leave from the Federal Reserve Board to assist General Hodge in Korea.
subfiles.title: Letter from General Hilldring to M. S. Szymczak Requesting Leave Extension for Bunce

subfiles.about: Inquires whether Edith M. Royce is interested in a position on the Bunce staff in Korea.
subfiles.summary: Snight inquires whether Royce is interested in an immediate position with the Bunce staff in Korea.
subfiles.title: Telegram Inquiring about Edith M. Royce's Interest in Bunce Staff Position

subfiles.about: Designates a record replacement copy of a telegram from CG USAFIK for central files.
subfiles.summary: Permanent record replacement sheet designating white copy of incoming USAFIK telegram for central filing.
subfiles.title: Document Record Replacement Sheet for Telegram from CG USAFIK

subfiles.about: Urges assignment of Shute and Royce and announces trip to Washington to recruit specialists.
subfiles.summary: Bunce urges immediate assignment of Shute and Royce, planning to visit Washington to select civilian specialists.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Bunce Requesting Personnel for Korea Staff

subfiles.about: Reports Bunce's departure for Washington and names Kinney acting mission head.
subfiles.summary: Langdon reports Bunce left Seoul by air for Washington, leaving Kinney in charge of the Economic Mission.
subfiles.title: Telegram 72 Reporting Bunce Departure for Washington

subfiles.about: Requests a War Department advance of $102,750 for the Economic Advisory Mission to Korea.
subfiles.summary: Kurth requests a $102,750 working fund advance from the War Department to maintain the Korea Economic Advisory Mission for fiscal year 1947.
subfiles.title: Letter from H. M. Kurth to Major General G. J. Richards on Korea Mission Funds

subfiles.about: Unfinished State Department telegram form stamped July 10, 1946.
subfiles.summary: Blank outgoing telegram form bearing date stamps and fragmentary typed text.
subfiles.title: Partial Outgoing Telegram Form

subfiles.about: Suggests Edith M. Royce travel to Washington for administrative training before proceeding to Korea.
subfiles.summary: Snight advises Royce to report to Washington for administrative training while awaiting overseas transportation.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Eldridge A. Snight to Edith M. Royce on Administrative Training

subfiles.about: Confirms travel orders and passport dispatch for Edith M. Royce.
subfiles.summary: Snight confirms Royce's travel orders from New York to San Francisco and forwards her passport.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Eldridge A. Snight to Edith M. Royce on Travel Orders

subfiles.about: Transmits bi-monthly lists of economic reports prepared by GHQ SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Burnett transmits lists of economic reports received by SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section, noting single-copy constraints in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 540 Transmitting List of SCAP Economic Reports

subfiles.about: Recommends forwarding Albert H. Mackenzie's intelligence notes to the Political Adviser in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Suggests pouching Mackenzie's interrogation notes to the Political Adviser in Tokyo for appropriate citation.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip Concerning Albert H. Mackenzie Letter

subfiles.about: Submits wartime intelligence notes from Peiping and inquires about diplomatic missions to Russia.
subfiles.summary: Mackenzie forwards rewritten 1945 FEA interrogation notes from Peiping and inquires about possible openings for State Department missions to Russia.
subfiles.title: Letter from Albert H. Mackenzie to John Carter Vincent Regarding China Interrogations
